reports.title: Q3 2026 Upstate NY cabin with views of fall foliage

lines: Q4 2026 • We expect to generate revenue of $3.22 billion to $3.28 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 16% to 18%, inclusive of an approximate two percentage point FX tailwind after factoring in our hedging program.
Adjusted EBITDA Margin in Q3 2026 was 52%, compared to 50% in Q3 2025.5 For the full-year 2026, we expect our effective tax rate to be in the mid-teens.

desk.headline: Revenue up 19% to $4.9bn, beat; full-year growth and margin outlook raised, new $12bn buyback
results: Revenue grew 19% (16% excluding currency) to $4.9bn and diluted EPS rose to $3.16 from $2.21, helped by a lower tax charge.
Bookings accelerated: nights and seats rose 16% to 155.0m and booking value 21% to $27.7bn, with growth in every region.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 22% to $2.5bn, lifting the margin to 52% from 50%; support cost per booking fell over 17%.
Free cash flow was $1.4bn; $0.7bn of shares were bought back and a new $12bn buyback was announced on top of the $2.7bn left.
The share of revenue taken from bookings dipped to 17.6% as more guests book early and pay later.

guidance.summary: Airbnb raised its 2026 outlook for both revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA margin, and guided Q4 revenue up 16–18%. Earlier ranges below are as reported from the call.

points: Booking growth sped up from Q2 in all four regions; pay-later bookings added about 3 points to nights, a lift expected to shrink in Q4.
The Q4 outlook assumes no lasting hit from unrest in Europe or the Middle East conflict, which management is monitoring.
Airbnb plans to start rolling out its own trip-planning AI agent in the first half of 2027; about 40% of support issues are now solved without a person.
Hotels are growing much faster than homes from a small base, and the new American Express tie-up is bringing in first-time guests.
Some marketing spend moved into Q4, which partly explains the slightly lower Q4 margin guide.
call.source: Shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1) and call coverage: MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance, 5 Nov 2026

watch: Whether booking growth holds as the pay-later boost fades in Q4.
Any demand impact from unrest in Europe or the Middle East.
Progress on hotels, services and the AI agent launch planned for H1 2027.
